data.content_ref: inline:The target asks for evidence within a single evaluation that distinguishes a genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. SRC_001 provides a causal mechanism for why the checklist might improve reliability (preventing premature closure via redundant binary verification), but it never identifies any evidence that would separate a true gain from coincidental compliance. Its counterconditions (incomplete checklist, groupthink) are generic failure modes, not diagnostic contrasts. It omits the precise distinction the problem demands: e.g., comparing checklist-driven panels on outcome-orthogonal checklist items, or probing whether the panel would still endorse the right answer when checklist steps are perturbed, to tell true reliability from right-answer-tracking-by-checklist-construction.
